How Insurers Use AI in Auditing to Fix Property Data Errors, with Overture Maps Foundation CTO

2026-08-06 Michael Shashoua, Digital Insurance Overture Maps Foundation, property data, AI auditing, insurance, computer vision, synthetic data, coordinate accuracy, Amy Rose, SAS, Agentech
Read the source article

Quick summary

Insurance industry experts including Overture Maps Foundation CTO Amy Rose explain how AI-powered tools — computer vision, synthetic data, and normalization — are being used to reconcile property data mismatches between addresses and map coordinates for accurate risk assessment.

Key takeaways

  • Property data mismatches occur when an address says "123 Main Street" but the map coordinates plot it elsewhere — insurers must determine which source is accurate
  • Amy Rose, CTO of Overture Maps Foundation, emphasizes that the power lies in auditability: communicating data issues so end users (human or machine) can perform proper validations
  • Insurance companies use computer vision and synthetic data generation to reconcile differing information about property risks, terrain, and historic claims
  • Synthetic data lets insurers augment datasets to respond to emerging risks and secondary perils worsened by climate change
  • Data-sourcing rules — "source of truth" and recency rules — help address discrepancies by establishing which data source takes precedence in conflicts
  • AI can normalize unstructured data by interpreting documents and reports, understanding that terms like "pipe jack" and "pipe boot" refer to the same thing
